sections.overview: The chestnut-capped babbler is a resident Asian songbird of the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.
sections.identification: Its common names refer to the chestnut-coloured crown that distinguishes this babbler.
sections.habitat: It uses dense scrub, tall grass and reedbeds, often in damp lowlands and secondary growth; it is also recorded in tea estates.
sections.diet: It feeds mainly on insects, gleaning among foliage and dense vegetation.
sections.behavior: It is described as diurnal and resident, foraging low in cover rather than making long seasonal movements.
sections.reproduction: Nesting information remains sparse in the consulted regional accounts.
sections.ecology: Its use of wet grass, reeds and scrub ties it to lowland cover, including some human-modified habitats.
sections.conservation: Bangladesh assessed it as Least Concern in 2014; that national assessment is not a substitute for a current global status.
